title: Edge prefetching session proxy — idea pad
body:
Quick pitch / one-liner:
A lightweight session proxy that runs near edge regions and proactively pulls (or salvages) model KV/prefix state for active user sessions so that cold-start decode latency on short-turn conversations and bursty chat workloads drops substantially without requiring full model copies at every edge node.

Context / why this: 
- We see many customers with conversational UIs where 90% of requests are short (1-3 new messages) but they still pay the p99 latency hit when KV state is fetched from centralized Dedicated/private pods or origin.
- Dedicated solutions can centralize throughput but latency-sensitive apps (support chat, real-time tools) could benefit from a tiny adjacency cache.
- Hosted latency SLOs sometimes break on user spikes when sessions are rehydrated from cold storage.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Reduce tail decode latency for rehydrated sessions by ~30-60ms 95/99p depending on model/region.
- Keep added infra cost minimal (favor small LRU caches + async prefetching vs full model replicas).
- Respect customer data residency and privacy constraints (no session content replication outside allowed regions).
- Make behavior configurable per-tenant (on/off, hints, budget).

High-level design ideas:
1) Session proxy process runs in edge PoPs (could be as lightweight container or sidecar in private env).
2) Proxy observes traffic patterns and maintains mini KV cache for sessions that meet affinity heuristics (recently active, high frequency). Cache stores compressed KV blobs (quantized/compressed checkpoint of KV cache / prefix tokens or a hashed delta).
3) Two fetch strategies: (a) On-demand warm: when a request arrives and session not in local cache, proxy asks origin for minimal 'hydration bundle' (recent KV snapshot, token boundaries) — origin can return compressed diff or pointer to CDN; (b) Predictive prefetch: proxy subscribes to session activity signal stream (heartbeat or websocket) and prefetches probable sessions into local cache proactively.
4) Fallback: if hydration fails or region not allowed, route directly to origin; must preserve correctness.
5) Control-plane: tenant-level policy to allow/deny edge prefetch per deployment (hosted true/false, private flag), TTL, max cached sessions, size budget.

API / wire sketches (rough):
- New header from client: X-Session-Affinity: session-id (existing) + optional X-Edge-Session-Mode: eager|lazy|none (client hint).
- Proxy <-> origin: POST /session/hydrate {session_id, max_kv_bytes, last_seq} -> {kv_blob_url, kv_blob_base64, compression:zstd, checksum}
- Telemetry tag: edge_prefetch=1, retrieve_time_ms, hydrate_size_bytes

User stories: 
- As a product engineer building a chat UI, I want 95th percentile response times to drop for re-opened sessions so users feel immediate continuity.
- As an SRE, I want to cap edge memory use per-tenant and quickly revoke caches when budget exceeded.
- As an enterprise customer, I want prefetching disabled by default and allowed only if my org permits session replication across certain regions.

Metrics to track / success signals:
- 95p/99p latency delta (decode + first-byte) for sessions with and without edge prefetch.
- Hydration hit rate (local cache hit %) and prefetch precision (prefetched but unused %).
- Cost metric: additional bandwidth/egress for hydration vs savings in origin GPU time.
- Error/fallback rate and privacy violations (sessions hydrated in disallowed regions).

Experiments / phases:
Phase 0: PoC on single region (us-west) using a proxy container colocated with CDN POP. Synthetic replay of chat sessions. Goal: validate that KV blobs compress well and reduce decode time.
Phase 1: Limited internal A/B test against small set of customers. Measure hit rate and latency improvements. Tune TTLs and heuristics.
Phase 2: Add tenant-level controls in Console + audit logs. Expand multi-region.
Phase 3: Run canary on dedicated customers where Private flags are enabled, verify compliance.

Heuristics ideas (how to pick sessions to cache):
- Recency: last message <= 30m (configurable).
- Turn frequency: sessions with >= 2 messages in last 5m.
- Size-first: only cache sessions with KV size <= X KB to avoid storing massive contexts.
- Behavioral hints: clients can set a privilege flag when session will be reopened soon (e.g., mobile app going background/foreground).

Implementation challenges / unknowns:
- How to represent a portable "hydration bundle" across model versions and quantization formats? Need standard protocol and versioning.
- Security: encrypt KV blobs at rest and in-transit; keys must respect tenant KMS boundaries. For private deployments, ensure KV stays in allowed networks.
- Cost tradeoffs: prefetch bandwidth vs saved origin decode time; likely depends on session length distribution.
- Consistency: when session updated on origin, invalidation or version pin required. Might use sequence numbers and optimistic hydration.
- Size: some models' KV caches grow fast — may need partial checkpoints (e.g., only last N layers or last M tokens).

Open questions (for next sync):
- How big are typical KV blobs for our most common short-convo models (gpt-like 7B/13B) under typical prompts? Need empirical snapshot.
- Should hydration be incremental (layer/delta) or full snapshot? Tradeoffs.
- Do we prefer client hints vs purely traffic-driven heuristics? Hybrid?
- SLA implications: if proxy introduces additional failure modes, how do we present in console?

Risks & mitigations:
- Privacy/regulatory: mitigate with strict tenant opts + region allowlists.
- Complexity: start with single-mode (lazy on-demand warm) then add predictive prefetch later.
- Cost blowup: implement per-tenant budget enforcement and eviction policies; default conservative TTLs.

Possible MVP acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end PoC that can hydrate a session into an edge proxy and reduce median/95p first-byte latency by measurable amount in lab (e.g., 25ms 95p improvement for test traffic).
- Config flag per-tenant to enable/disable prefetch and a console toggle in feature flags.
- Audit logs emitted for every hydration event with region and size.

Next steps (immediate):
- Data ask: sample KV size distribution for top 5 hosted models over last 30 days (by session frequency). Assign to Maya.
- Quick spike: build minimal proxy that can request a blob and serve it back into a local runtime (no full model exec) to measure hydration cost. Assign to Evan.
- Add initial design note to Confluence and link GH#1289. Owner: me (Jordan).

Notes to self / throwaway ideas:
- Could combine with prefix caching for embeddings-heavy requests: store combined lightweight prefix + short-term semantic cache for retrieval-augmented convos.
- Consider integrating with our existing KV compression work (quantized checkpoints).
- Maybe offer "session warm credits" in billing so customers can opt-in to keep N sessions warm at fixed monthly charge.

End of pad. Will iterate after the data spike.
